conf.description: printers-mfd device-security-syslog dataset, syslog-cef format (Xerox AltaLink/VersaLink SIEM branch): CEF header+extension decode via regex_extract+serde kvp (the built-in cef function's conf shape could not be validated live -- see README), sharing the mfd.* schema with the HP and csv-file branches.

conf.comment: printers-mfd / device-security-syslog / syslog-cef: Xerox AltaLink/VersaLink SIEM feed, RFC5424 syslog wrapper carrying a CEF-formatted MSG (facility 13, Log Audit). No stock 'cef' function ships a working extract-mode conf here: an empty conf throws a runtime 'Missing headers' error and both 'source' and 'mode' are rejected as unknown properties by live validation, so per the never-guess-a-key-name rule this uses regex_extract (verified shape) for the CEF pipe-delimited header plus serde kvp for the extension, not the cef function -- see README for the evidence. PRI supplies only log.syslog.facility.code; the CEF Severity header is authoritative for log.syslog.severity.code (both target the same ECS name in the map, so PRI's severity is not recomputed, avoiding two writers of one field). Shares mfd.* and event.dataset with this dataset's HP and csv-file branches so all three land in one Elastic data stream.

functions.description: record why the cef function was not used (live-validation evidence) and the PRI/Severity de-duplication decision
split the syslog PRI/timestamp/hostname header and the CEF pipe-delimited header fields from the extension block
extract the CEF extension key=value pairs (dvchost, deviceExternalId, suser, duser, spriv, src, dst, request, sproc, outcome, reason, msg, xrxaccUID1, xrxaccAID1)
batch-rename the straight-copy status:mapped/partial fields to their ECS targets

decompose PRI's facility code, invert Severity into event.severity, split/recognise suser as realm-prefixed or an email address, wrap spriv as a one-element user.roles array, gate source/destination.ip on looking like an address, fold event.outcome, and route the Xerox accounting IDs to mfd.accounting.*
set Cribl's canonical event time from the syslog header's already-RFC3339 timestamp (never write @timestamp directly)
tag the event with its dataset (shared with the HP and csv-file branches; no hyphens per the Elastic data-stream naming constraint)
Re-nest flat dotted keys (data-maps canonical step)
